device.name: Quantinuum H2-2 (System Model H2)

qubits.quote: Experiments were performed on the Quantinuum H2-2 trapped ion processor, which provides 56 qubits with all-to-all connectivity, mid-circuit measurement and reset.

qubits_used.quote: Our gadget experiments utilised 27 qubits of which there were 10 data qubits, 10 ancilla qubits to perform stabiliser checks, and 7 qubits for the gadget (3 gadget qubits, 4 gadget checks), while our memory experiments required 20 qubits.
qubits_used.source: arXiv:2610.39067 Sec. III.B; confirmed by required_num_qubits=27/20 in the QIR

gate_zones.quote: By using a greedy scheduling of the 4 gate zones for the R=3 circuit we estimate a single shot to require ~500 ms

gate_zones.quote: System Model H2 has 56 physical qubits (ions) that move, individually or in pairs, between four interaction zones where all quantum operations (initialization, measurement, single-, and two-qubit gates) are performed using lasers.

gate_zones.note: physical gate zones, of which 4 (DG) do quantum operations
gate_zones.quote: Random qubit access utilizes all 8 gate zones as swapping regions. ... State Preparation and Measurement (SPAM) is only possible in the 4 gate zones.
H2 is currently configured with 4 active gate zones, the two-qubit (2Q) gates are executed in 7 batches of 4 parallel gates.

program.pipeline_quote: We first create each circuit in Stim with a gate set of {Measure, Reset, H, X, CNOT}. We then use the PyTKET library to rebase and optimise the circuit to be compatible with Quantinuum H2 hardware. The circuit compiled to the H2-2 device consists of {Measure, Reset, Rx, Rz, ZZPhase(0.5)} operations with rotations of multiples of π/2 angles, hence this is still a Clifford circuit. The circuit is optimised using TKET optimisation level 2. Finally, we use Q# to convert to Quantum Intermediate Representation (QIR).
program.input_format: LLVM-IR text (QIR adaptive profile) saved with a .json extension; a single basic block, no branching; calls __quantum__qis__{reset,rz,rx,rzz,m}__body and __quantum__rt__result_record_output
program.output_format: microsoft.quantum-results.v2 JSON; Results[0].Shots is the time-ordered list of shots; each shot lists bits in the order of the result_record_output calls (labels k_a(k-1)r) = the original Stim measurement order. Results[0].Histogram aggregates identical shots.

gate_map.h2_native: Rxy(3π/2, 0) (≡ Rxy(π/2, π) up to phase)
Measure (Z basis, qubit left in the measured state)

program.angles_present: only multiples of π/2: rz ∈ {π/2, 3π/2}, rx ∈ {π/2, π, 3π/2}, rzz ∈ {π/2}

qubit_roles.0-4: ancilla of X stabiliser S_X,j (j = qubit)
qubit_roles.5-14: data qubit q_i (i = qubit - 5); left block q0-q4, right block q5-q9
qubit_roles.15-19: ancilla of Z stabiliser S_Z,j (j = qubit - 15)
qubit_roles.20,21,22: kappa_2, kappa_3, kappa_4 (X1 gadget qubits); reused as nu_0, nu_1, nu_2 (Z2 gadget, SEQ)
qubit_roles.23: gamma_0 gauge check (X1 gadget); reused as lambda (Z2 gadget X-type gauge check, SEQ)
qubit_roles.24,25,26: chi_2, chi_3, chi_7 (X1 gadget checks); reused as eta_2, eta_6, eta_7 (Z2 gadget checks, SEQ)

program.code: [[10,2,3]] generalised bicycle, l=5, a(x)=1+x^2, b(x)=1+x, H_X=[A|B], H_Z=[B^T|A^T]; X1=X(q2,q3,q7), X2=X(q1,q7,q9), Z1=Z(q2,q4,q5), Z2=Z(q2,q6,q7)

XR1, XR1-MinusMinus, XR3: L0 X1,G = chi_2 chi_3 chi_7 of merged cycle 1
L1 X1,D = X(q2 q3 q7) final data
L2 X2,D = X(q1 q7 q9) final data
XR1-ZeroZero, XR1-OneOne: L0 X1,G xor X1,D (X1,G alone is random for Z-basis preparations)
SEQ, SEQ-OneOne: L0 Z2,G = eta_2 eta_6 eta_7 * m(kappa_2)
L1 Z2,D = Z(q2 q6 q7) final data * m(kappa_2)

decoding.method: offline Tesseract (most-likely-error, search-based) on the Stim detector error model, short-beam configuration
decoding.quote: Decoding is performed offline with the Tesseract most-likely-error decoder acting on the detector error model generated by Stim. ... Specifically, we configure the decoder to the short beam parameters as described in Ref. [Beni2025Tesseract].
decoding.decoder_ref: Aghababaie Beni, Higgott, Shutty, 'Tesseract: A Search-Based Decoder for Quantum Error Correction', arXiv:2503.10988
decoding.statistics_quote: Logical error rates are bounded in equal-tailed 95% Jeffreys credible intervals.
decoding.verification_quote: A logical state of the two encoded qubits is prepared then verified on trivial outcome of the initial bare code syndrome extraction round (SE1).
decoding.here: Tesseract is not installed in this environment (not installed, to leave the environment unchanged); verify.py uses PyMatching (decompose_errors=True works for all DEMs) and a sampled lookup-table decoder as a sanity check.

XR1_X1G.quote: A single-round surgery measurement using seven gadget qubits measures the X1 operator with a 0.72 [0.32, 1.41]% (95% credible interval) error rate and agrees with subsequent transversal measurement with 1.03 [0.60, 1.65]% error.

XR3_X1G.quote: For the XR3 gadget circuit, only |++>_L was prepared, with 0 errors in 957 verification passing shots consistent with simulation and upper bounding the error rate at 0.26% in a 95% credible interval.

XR3_unverified.quote: We note that the XR3 error rate depends entirely on the verification step, without verification there are 10 errors in 1000 shots.

XR3_spectator.quote: disagrees in 2/957 verified shots for the three round circuit (error rate 0.21 [0.04, 0.67]%)

XR3_no_chi_detectors.quote: Decoding without the chi detectors results in 7/957 errors (error rate 0.73 [0.33, 1.43]%)

SEQ_Z2G.quote: Averaging over preparation in |00>_L and |11>_L the Z2 gadget measurement disagrees with preparation in 11/978 verified shots, with error rate 1.12 [0.60, 1.94]%.

exactness: EXACT: gate sequence, gate angles, qubit indices, reset/measure positions — the Stim instruction list equals the QIR instruction list one-for-one (checked in verify.py §2).
EXACT up to global phase: rz/rx/rzz(kπ/2) ↔ Stim S/Z/S_DAG, SQRT_X/X/SQRT_X_DAG, SQRT_ZZ (checked numerically, verify.py §1).
EXACT: measurement record index = QIR %Result id (results are allocated in program order; asserted); output-array position → record index from the result_record_output calls.
DERIVED: TICK placement (sequential packing of program order; the QIR has no layers). TICKs carry no timing.
DERIVED: QUBIT_COORDS(q, 0) = program index on a line; H2 has no fixed qubit geometry (ions are transported).

RECONSTRUCTED from the paper's definitions: detectors and observables. Bulk/boundary/fusion detector rates reproduce the paper's tables tab:fusion and tab:max_rates exactly, and SE1 verification reproduces every post-verification shot count.
INFERRED: the 5-body 'product of all S_Z (S_X) in SE1' detector, added so the detector set spans all deterministic parities and the XR3 count equals the paper's 62.

CHOICE: X1,G uses the chi outcomes of merged cycle 1 (paper Fig. timeline (App. A, fig:gadget_3_round) marks R=1 as the non-destructive measurement); with chi repetition detectors any cycle is equivalent.
NOT EXACT/UNKNOWN: the original pre-TKET Stim circuits are not published (Zenodo has only QIR + results); hardware transport, timing and zone assignment are not public.
